subject: Request: EU-only processing evidence + retention/deletion timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Browne <sarah.browne@nexahealth.eu>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Keller <thomas.keller@nexahealth.eu>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: EU-only processing - evidence and deletion/retention questions

Hi Aditya,

As part of our procurement and legal review for NexaHealth's pilot we need a compact evidence bundle showing that Redwood can perform in-region (EU) processing and provide deletion/retention proof in line with Schrems II + SCCs expectations. Specific asks from our security and legal teams: 

- Confirmation that inference and all persistent storage for our tenant can be restricted to EU regions (including backups) and where operator access is limited.
- Sample retention-deletion matrix showing how long artifacts are kept (logs, prompts, KV cache, model artifacts) and deletion workflows.
- Evidence of the SCCs implementation (where Annex references live) and whether Redwood will sign customer-specific Annexes.
- For encrypted data-at-rest, does Redwood support customer-managed KMS in EU (Y/N) and a short note on key separation for operators.

Can you share a timeline for providing these items and any standard artifacts you already use (attestations, operator access snapshots)? We are aiming to complete this review within two weeks.

Appreciate a clear list so we can forward to Legal.

Best,
Sarah
Security Lead, NexaHealth
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Browne <sarah.browne@nexahealth.eu>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing - evidence and deletion/retention questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: yes, we can support EU-only inference and retention/deletion evidence; below is what we'll produce and a proposed timeline. I'll loop in our privacy and ops leads (cc'ed) to confirm details.

Deliverables (planned):
- In-region processing attestation (PDF) — confirms inference + persistent storage and backups scoped to EU regions.
- Retention & deletion matrix (XLSX) — artifact-by-artifact retention windows, trigger conditions, and deletion workflow steps.
- Operator access snapshot (PDF) — sample audit showing role-based access lists and recent operator activity (redacted).
- SCCs implementer guidance & Annex index (PDF) — where to find Annex references and standard text; note on customer-specific Annex acceptance.
- KMS options doc (short) — details on customer-managed KMS in EU and key separation for operator accounts.

Proposed timeline:
- Initial bundle (attestation + retention matrix + SCCs index): 5 business days (by 2026-11-19)
- Operator audit snapshot and KMS notes: additional 3 business days (by 2026-11-24)

Attachments I will share in the initial email: retention-deletion-matrix.xlsx and SCCs_Annexes_Index.pdf. Naomi / Lauren / Irene — can you confirm we are comfortable with the 5/3 business day split and whether Legal needs any extra items for NexaHealth?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing - evidence and deletion/retention questions

+1 on the timeline from my side. A few operational clarifications to include in the bundle so Sarah's team has what they need: 

- Backups: we have a 14-day rolling snapshot retention by default; for EU-only customers we can restrict snapshot storage to the EU and provide a deletion certificate for snapshots older than retention window.
- KV/cache behavior: ephemeral by default for inference; persistent KV only for customers who opt in — show opt-in record in the matrix.
- Deletion proof: we can provide a deletion runbook and an operator-executed erasure log (sha256 hashes) for object store deletions.
- SCCs: we will attach the standard Annex index. If NexaHealth requires customer-specific Annex modifications we should escalate to Legal — that typically takes longer (2–3 weeks).

One ask for Aditya: flag any current customers with tight KMS workflows (we have a small list) so we can include language about customer-managed keys and split-ownership.

Irene — can you pull the latest operator-audit snapshot (redacted) and confirm we can deliver it by 2026-11-19?

-N
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Browne <sarah.browne@nexahealth.eu>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Keller <thomas.keller@nexahealth.eu>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing - evidence and deletion/retention questions

Thanks, Aditya and Naomi — that scope sounds good. A couple of follow-ups from my infra team before you prepare the bundle: 

- Backups: we need confirmation that backups are encrypted with customer-managed KMS (if we choose that option) and that keys never leave the EU. Are split-ownership / KMS escrow options available?
- Operator access: can you confirm whether operator SSH/RDP access is ever used for debugging in EU-only tenants, and if so whether access events are captured in the audit snapshot you mentioned?
- SLA exception: if deletion proofs take 3–4 business days to generate, will that satisfy our compliance checks?

If you can include short, plain-language answers to those three questions in the initial bundle that'd be ideal.

Best,
Sarah
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Browne <sarah.browne@nexahealth.eu>, Thomas Keller <thomas.keller@nexahealth.eu>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-only processing - evidence and deletion/retention questions

Hi Sarah / Thomas — thanks for the clarifying questions. Attached is the initial evidence bundle and short answers to the infra questions. Quick summary below and notes on next steps. Attachments: SCCs_Annexes_Index.pdf, retention-deletion-matrix.xlsx, operator-access-audit-snapshot-20261113.pdf 

Short answers (plain language):
1) KMS & backups: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) with keys hosted in EU KMS providers (AWS KMS EU regions, GCP KMS EU locations). Keys can be configured so key material never leaves the EU. We do not provide KMS escrow by default; split-ownership arrangements can be discussed with Legal (likely a contractual addendum).

2) Operator access for debugging: For EU-only tenants operator access is limited to role-based API actions. We do not provision direct SSH/RDP into customer VMs for hosted Redwood instances. On rare occasions where deeper debugging is required for Dedicated or Private deployments, temporary access workflows are used and all access is logged and approved via the access-request process. Those events are included in the operator-access-audit-snapshot (attached), with timestamps and redacted operator IDs.

3) Deletion proof SLA: We can generate deletion evidence and a signed certificate of erasure within 3 business days for standard object-store deletions and index/table purges. For complex cases (deep backups, long-term archival) timelines can extend — we'll flag those in the matrix.

Next steps: 
- I've uploaded the artifacts to a shared Drive folder and added a short README at the top level: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNexaEvidence
- If NexaHealth is happy with the standard Annex text, Legal can proceed with SCCs signature. If they want Annex edits, please flag and I'll involve our Legal team (turnaround ~2 weeks).

If helpful, Naomi / Lauren — can you join a 30-minute call with Sarah/Thomas next week to walk through the operator snapshot? I'll propose times after I get confirmation.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SCCs_Annexes_Index.pdf (PDF), retention-deletion-matrix.xlsx (XLSX), operator-access-audit-snapshot-20261113.pdf (PDF)
